response:
It is completely normal to feel anxious before starting therapy, but please know that you do not need to worry about crying. Therapists are professionals who see people cry all the time—in fact, their offices are usually stocked with tissues for exactly this reason. Crying is a natural release of emotion and a very common, healthy part of the healing process. 

Your therapist will not judge you or think less of you if you cry. They are there to provide a safe, supportive space for you to express whatever you are feeling, whether that involves tears, frustration, or even silence. You can even tell them in your first session that you are nervous about crying; sharing that fear can often help relieve the pressure. You are taking a brave step by starting counseling, and it is entirely okay to just be yourself and let your emotions out.
